questions.q: If the collision frequency of hydrogen molecules in a closed chamber at $27^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}} \mathrm{C}$ is $\mathrm{Z}$, then the collision frequency of the same system at $127^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}} \mathrm{C}$ is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Assuming mean free path constant.
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{f} \propto \mathrm{V} \propto \sqrt{\mathrm{T}} \\ & \frac{\mathrm{f}_1}{\mathrm{f}_2}=\sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{T}_1}{\mathrm{~T}_2}}=\sqrt{\frac{300}{400}} \\ & \mathrm{f}_2=\sqrt{\frac{4}{3}}=\mathrm{f}_1=\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}} \mathrm{Z}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The mean free path and the average speed of oxygen molecules at 300 K and 1 atm are $3 \times 10^{-7} \mathrm{~m}$ and $600 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ respectively. Find the frequency of its collisions.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \text { Frequency }=\frac{1}{T}=\frac{V_{\text {avg }}}{\lambda} \\ & =\frac{600}{3 \times 157}=2 \times 10^9 \mathrm\sec^{-1}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The internal energy  \left(U\right)$, pressure  \left(P\right)$ and volume  \left(V\right)$ of an ideal gas are related as $U = 3PV + 4 .$& The gas is$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$U = 3PV + 4$

$\dfrac{nf}{2}RT = 3PV + 4$

$\dfrac{f}{2}PV = 3PV + 4$

$f = 6 + \dfrac{8}{PV}$

Since degree of freedom is more than $6$& therefore gas is polyatomic

questions.q: The temperature at which the kinetic energy of oxygen molecules becomes double than its value at $27 ° C$ is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The kinetic energy is given by& $KE = \dfrac{f}{2}kT$.

Let the kinetic energy be~${K}_{1}$~at~$27 ° C$~and the kinetic energy be~$K '$~at~$T '$~temperature. As given in the question,~$K ' = 2{K}_{1}$. Hence,~

$\dfrac{K '}{K1} = \dfrac{T '}{T} ⇒ 2 = \dfrac{T '}{300} ⇒ T ' = 600K$

In Celsius the temperature is~$T ' - 273 = 327 ° C$.

questions.q: A vessel contains $16g$ of hydrogen and $128g$ of oxygen at standard temperature and pressure. The volume of the vessel in ${cm}^{3}$ is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Number of moles of Hydrogen \left({H}_{2}\right) = \dfrac{m}{M} = \dfrac{16}{2} = 8$

Number of moles of oxygen~\left({O}_{2}\right) = \dfrac{128}{32} = 4$

Using ideal gas equation,~$PV = nRT$,

Where pressure~$P = 1atm = 1 . 01 \times {10}^{5}Pa \left(STP\right)$

Putting the values,~

$1 . 01 \times {10}^{5}V = \left(8 + 4\right) \times8 . 314 \times273$

$V = $\dfrac{12 \times 8 . 314 \times 273}{1 . 01 \times {10}^{5}}$m^{3}$

$= 0 . 27 \times {10}^{6}{cm}^{3} =27 \times {10}^{4}{cm}^{3}

$

questions.q: A $25 \times {10}^{- 3}m^{3}$ volume cylinder is filled with $1$ mol of ${O}_{2}$ gas at room temperature $( 300K )$ . The molecular diameter of ${O}_{2}$ , and its root mean square speed, are found to be $0.3$ nm and $200m / s$ , respectively. What is the average collision rate (per second) for an ${O}_{2}$ molecule?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Average collision rate $= n\overset{-}{v}d^{2}\pi$
$= \dfrac{6.023 \times {10}^{23}}{25 \times {10}^{- 3}} \times \sqrt{\dfrac{8}{3\pi}} \times 200 \times {\left(0.3 \times {10}^{- 9}\right)}^{2}\pi \approx 4 \times {10}^{- 12}$

questions.q: The number density of molecules of a gas depends on their distance r from the origin as, $n\left(r\right) = {n}_{0}e^{- \alphar^{4}} .$ Then the numer of molecules is proportional to:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Density of molecules of gas as a of r is, $n ( r ) = {n}_{0}e^{- \alphar^{4}}$
Total no. of molecules $= \mathop{∫}_{0}^{∞}n ( r ) dv$
$\mathop{∫}_{0}^{\infty}{n}_{0}e^{- \alphar^{4}}4\pir^{2}dr$
To integrate this, substitute $u = {\alpha}^{3 / 4}r^{3}$ this will give us $dr = \dfrac{1}{3{\alpha}^{3 / 4}r^{2}}du$
Now, the integration will become, $\dfrac{4\pi{n}_{0}}{3{\alpha}^{3 / 4}}\mathop{∫}_{0}^{\infty}e^{- u^{4 / 3}}du$
This shows that the numer of molecules is proportional to ${n}_{0}{\alpha}^{- 3 / 4}$

questions.q: At $300K$, the rms speed of oxygen molecules is~$\sqrt{\dfrac{\alpha + 5}{α}}$~times to that of its average speed in the~gas. Then, the value of~$\alpha$ will be (use~$\pi = \dfrac{22}{7}$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
RMS speed is given by,& ${v}_{rms} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3RT}{M}}$~and average speed is given by,~${v}_{avg} = \sqrt{\dfrac{8}{π}\dfrac{RT}{M}}$.

As per question,

${v}_{rms} = \sqrt{\dfrac{\alpha + 5}{α}}{v}_{avg}$

$⇒ \sqrt{\dfrac{3RT}{M}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{\alpha + 5}{α}}\sqrt{\dfrac{8}{π}\dfrac{RT}{M}}$

$⇒ 3 = \dfrac{\alpha + 5}{α} \times \dfrac{8}{\dfrac{22}{7}}$

$⇒ \alpha = 28$

questions.q: Two moles of a monoatomic gas is mixed with six moles of a diatomic gas. The molar specific heat of the mixture at constant volume is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For mixture of gases, we can write

${C}_{v} = \dfrac{{n}_{1}{C}_{v1} + {n}_{2}{C}_{v2}}{{n}_{1} + {n}_{2}}$

$= \dfrac{2 \times \dfrac{3}{2}R + 6 \times \dfrac{5}{2}R}{2 + 6}$

$= \dfrac{9}{4}R$

questions.q: What will be the average value of energy along one degree of freedom for an ideal gas in thermal equilibrium at a temperature $T ?$ (${k}_{B}$ is Boltzmann constant)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Energy associated with each degree of freedom per molecule $= \dfrac{1}{2}{k}_{B}T .$

Hence,~the average value of energy along one degree of freedom for an ideal gas in thermal equilibrium at a temperature $T =\dfrac{1}{2}{k}_{B}T .$

questions.q:
A mixture of hydrogen and oxygen has volume $2000{cm}^{3}$, temperature $300K$, pressure $100$ kPa and mass $0 . 76g$. The ratio of number of moles of hydrogen to number of moles of oxygen in the mixture will be

[Take gas constant $R = 8 . 3JK^{- 1}{mol}^{- 1}$]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
From the ideal gas equation, total number of moles in the mixture are,

$n = \dfrac{PV}{RT} = \dfrac{2 \times {10}^{- 3} \times 100 \times {10}^{3} \times 3}{25 \times 300}⇒ n = \dfrac{2}{25} = 0 . 08$

If number of moles of oxygen are ${n}_{1}$~and of~hydrogen are~${n}_{2}$

${n}_{1} + {n}_{2} = n = 0 . 08 \ldots \left(1\right)$

And total mass of the mixture

${n}_{1} \left(32\right) + {n}_{2} \left(2\right) = 0 . 76 \ldots \left(2\right)$

Solving the above equations,

${n}_{1} = 0 . 02$~and~${n}_{2} = 0 . 06$

\dfrac{n2}{n1} =$3$

questions.q:
Match the $\dfrac{\text{C}\text{p}}{\text{C}\text{v}}$ ratio for ideal gases with different type of molecules:

Molecule Type ${C}_{p} / {C}_{v}$
(A) Monoatomic (I)~$7 / 5$
(B) Diatomic rigid molecules (II)~$9 / 7$
(C) Diatomic non-rigid molecules (III)~$4 / 3$
(D) Triatomic rigid molecules (IV)~$5 / 3$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Relation between the ratio of specific heat and degree of freedom is given by,

$\gamma = 1 + \dfrac{2}{f} . . . ( 1 )$

For monoatomic molecule,~$A$,~$f = 3$

~$⇒ \gamma = 1 + \dfrac{2}{3} = \dfrac{5}{3}$

For diatomic rigid molecule~$B$,~$f = 5$

~$⇒ \gamma = 1 + \dfrac{2}{5} = \dfrac{7}{5}$

For diatomic non-rigid molecule~$C$,~$f = 7$~$⇒ \gamma = 1 + \dfrac{2}{7} = \dfrac{9}{7}$

For~Triatomic rigid molecule~$D$,~$f = 6$~$⇒ \gamma = 1 + \dfrac{2}{6} = \dfrac{4}{3}$

questions.q: The temperature of a gas having $2 . 0 \times {10}^{25}$ molecules per cubic meter at $1 . 38atm$ (Given, $k = 1 . 38 \times {10}^{- 23}JK^{- 1} )$ is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
From ideal gas equation, $PV = nRT$

$⇒ PV = \dfrac{N}{NA}RT$, where $N =$ total number of molecules

$⇒ P = \dfrac{N}{V}\left(\dfrac{R}{NA}\right)T ⇒ P = \dfrac{N}{V}kT$

$⇒ 1 . 38 \times \left(1 . 01 \times {10}^{5}\right) = \left(2 \times {10}^{25}\right) \times \left(1 . 38 \times {10}^{- 23}\right) \times T$

$⇒ 1 . 01 \times {10}^{5} = 2 \times {10}^{2} \times T$

$T = \dfrac{1 . 01 \times {10}^{3}}{2} \approx 500K$

questions.q: A flask contains argon and oxygen in the ratio of $3: 2$~in mass and the mixture is kept at $27 ° C$. The ratio of their average kinetic energy per molecule respectively
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given here,& $\dfrac{mAr}{mO} = \dfrac{3}{2}$.

As argon is monoatomic gas, so it has three degree of freedom \left(f\right)$~and oxygen is a diatomic gas, so its degree of freedom is five.

We know that average kinetic energy per molecule is given by~$KE = \dfrac{f}{2}kT$, where,~$k$~is Boltzmann's constant and~$T$~is temperature.

Here,~$T = 27 ° C$~is fixed for both gas.

So,~$\dfrac{\left(KE\right)Ar}{\left(KE\right)O} = \dfrac{\dfrac{3}{2}kT}{\dfrac{5}{2}kT} = \dfrac{3}{5}$

$

questions.q: A diatomic gas with rigid molecules does $10J$ of work when expanded at constant pressure. What would be the heat energy absorbed by the gas, in this process?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
${C}_{p} = \dfrac{7}{2}R$ (for diatomic gas)
$\Delta Q = n{C}_{p}\Delta T \left(∴ Isobaricprocess\right)$
$\Delta W = nR\Delta T = 10J$
Given
$∴ \Delta Q = n \times \ddfrac{7}{2}R\Delta$T = \dfrac{7}{2} \times10 = $35J\left\{nR\Delta$T = 10J\right\}$

questions.q: The number of air molecules per ${cm}^{3}$~is~increased from $3 \times {10}^{19}$~to $12 \times {10}^{19} .$ The ratio of collision frequency of air molecules before and after the increase in number respectively is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The given data is&

${n}_{1} = 3 \times {10}^{19}{n}_{2} = 12 \times {10}^{19}$

The mean time between two collision has the meaning of a period $τ$, since it indicates the repetitive time intervals in which on average collisions take place. The reciprocal of the time $τ$ can be understood as the~collision frequency$f$, which indicates the number of collisions per unit time.The collision frequency~is also directly proportional to the number molecules per unit volume.

$f ∝ \dfrac{1}{τ}$

$⇒ f ∝ n$

$⇒ \dfrac{f\text{1}}{f\text{2}} = \dfrac{n1}{n2} = \dfrac{3 \times {10}^{19}}{12 \times {10}^{19}} = 0 . 25$

questions.q: Two gases - argon (atomic radius $0.07nm,$ atomic weight $40$ ) and xenon (atomic radius $0.1nm,$ atomic weight $140$ ) have the same number density and are at the same temperature. The ratio of their respective mean free times is closest to:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Mean free time $= \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}n\pid^{2}{v}_{rms}}$
$\dfrac{{t}_{Ar}}{{t}_{Xe}} = \dfrac{{d}_{Xe}^{2}}{{d}_{Ar}^{2}} \times \sqrt{\dfrac{{m}_{1}}{{m}_{2}}}$
$= {\left(\dfrac{0.1}{0.07}\right)}^{2} \times \sqrt{\dfrac{40}{140}}$
$= \left(\dfrac{10}{7}\right)2 \times \sqrt{\dfrac{2}{7}} = 1.09$
closest value is~$1 . 83$

questions.q: For an ideal gas the instantaneous change in pressure $P$ with volume $V$ is given by the equation $\dfrac{dP}{dV} = - aP .$ If $P = {P}_{0}$ at $V = 0$ is the given boundary condition, then the maximum temperature one mole of gas can attain is:~(Here $R$ is the gas constant)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\dfrac{dP}{dV} = - aP$
${∫}_{P0}^{P}\dfrac{dP}{P} = - {∫}_{0}^{v}adV ⇒ ln\dfrac{P}{P0} = - aV$
$P = {P}_{0}e^{- aV}$
Now, $PV = RT$(as $n = 1$)
$P + V\dfrac{dP}{dV} = R\dfrac{dT}{dV}$
[~for maximum $T, \dfrac{dT}{dV} = 0$]
$P - aPV = 0 ⇒ V = \dfrac{1}{a}$
Thus, $T = \dfrac{PV}{R} = \dfrac{{P}_{0}e^{- 1}}{Ra} = \dfrac{P0}{eRa}$

questions.q: The root-mean-square speed of molecules of a given mass of a gas at $27 ° C$ and $1$ atmosphere pressure is $200ms^{- 1} .$~The root-mean-square speed of molecules of the gas at $127 ° C$ and $2$ atmosphere pressure is $\dfrac{x}{3}ms^{- 1} .$~The value of $x$ will be __________.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
${v}_{rms} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3RT}{M}}⇒ {v}_{rms} ∝ \sqrt{T}⇒ \dfrac{\left({v}_{rms}\right)2}{\left({v}_{rms}\right)1} = \sqrt{\dfrac{T2}{{T}_{1}}}= \sqrt{\dfrac{400}{300}}= \dfrac{2}{3}$

\left({v}_{rms}\right)2 = \dfrac{2}{3}\left({v}_{rms}\right)1= \dfrac{2}{3} \times 200⇒ \left({v}_{rms}\right)2 = \dfrac{400}{3}ms^{- 1}$.

$

questions.q: A closed vessel contains $0.1$ mole of a monoatomic ideal gas at $200\text{K}$. If $0.05$ mole of the same gas at $400K$ is added to it, the final equilibrium temperature (in $\text{K}$) of the gas in the vessel will be close to ______
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
\left(0 .1\right)\left(200\right) + \left(0 .05\right)\left(400\right) = \left(0 .15\right)T$

$T = \dfrac{20 + 20}{0 .15} = \dfrac{800}{3} = 266 .67$

$= 266 .67$

$

questions.q: When a gas filled in a closed vessel is heated by raising the temperature by $1 ° C$, its pressure increases by $0 . 4 %$ The initial temperature of the gas is _____~$K$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
From ideal gas equation,& $PV = nRT$, where,~$n$~is amount of substance,~$R$~is ideal gas constant and~$V$~is volume.

In closed vessel volume remains constant.

So, $\dfrac{dP}{P} \times 100 = \dfrac{dT}{T} \times 100$

$0 . 4 = \dfrac{1}{T} \times 100$

$⇒ T = 250K$

questions.q: \gamma_{\mathrm{A}}$ is the specific heat ratio of monoatomic gas A having 3 translational degrees of freedom. $\gamma_B$ is the specific heat ratio of polyatomic gas B having 3 translational, 3 rotational degrees of freedom and 1 vibrational mode. If $\frac{\gamma_{\mathrm{A}}}{\gamma_{\mathrm{B}}}= $\left(1+\frac{1}{\mathrm{n}}), then the value of $n$ is _______.$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \frac{\gamma_A}{\gamma_B}=\frac{\mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{A}}+2}{\mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{A}}} \times \frac{\mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{B}}}{\mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{B}}+2} \\ & =\frac{3+2}{3} \times \frac{(6+2)}{(6+2)+2} \\ & =\frac{5}{3} \times \frac{8}{10}=\frac{40}{30} \\ & \because \frac{40}{30}=1+\frac{1}{\mathrm{n}} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{40}{30}-1=\frac{1}{\mathrm{n}}\end{aligned}$
$\Rightarrow \mathrm{n}=3$

questions.q: One mole of a monoatomic gas is mixed with three moles of a diatomic gas. The molecular specific heat of mixture at constant volume is $\dfrac{\alpha2}{4}RJmolK^{- 1}$; then the value of $\alpha$ will be _____ . (Assume that the given diatomic gas has no vibrational mode.)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Molecular specific heat at constant volume in& terms of degrees of freedom& is given by& ${C}_{V} = \dfrac{f}{2}R$

Molecular specific heat of mixture at constant volume is~${C}_{V} / mix = \dfrac{{n}_{1}{C}_{V1} + {n}_{2}{C}_{V2}}{{n}_{1} + {n}_{2}}$

$= \dfrac{1 \times \dfrac{3R}{2} + 3 \times \dfrac{5R}{2}}{1 + 3}$

$= \dfrac{9R}{4} = \dfrac{\alpha2}{4}R$

$⇒ \alpha = 3$
